obligation: Phase B / S012 §26 -- pursue the representation frontier: does low-rank + correction reduce MLP active bytes below q3 at q3 quality (held-out)?
method: down_proj L31; real post_swiglu activations, TRAIN/TEST split; base(qN absmax g64) + activation-aware low-rank correction of the residual (RRR on train residual-output, generalizes); output rel-Frobenius error held-out vs q3; total bytes = base + rank-k f16 factors.

q3_plus_correction.note: GENERALIZES and beats q3 quality, but ADDS bytes -- a Matryoshka/quality lever (feeds G11), NOT a speed/byte-reduction lever

q2_plus_correction.note: q2 base (err 0.626) is too coarse -- correction CANNOT recover q3 quality (0.22) within a reasonable byte budget; still 0.36-0.40 at >=q3 bytes

verdict: MEASURED NEGATIVE for byte reduction. No low-rank + correction split beats q3's density-quality point: q2-base cannot be corrected back to q3 quality cheaply, and q3-base+correction is more bytes for better quality (Matryoshka, not speed). q3 is Pareto-optimal on the MLP density-quality frontier. The hybrid GENERALIZES (unlike pure low-rank) but does not move active bytes below q3 at q3 quality.
consequence: The representation wall is now COMPREHENSIVE across compression families -- pure low-rank (overfits), function low-rank (overfits held-out), hybrid low-rank+correction (this: Pareto-dominated by q3), entropy (stored-not-active), sparsity (~2x marginal), bit-descent (3.34 coherent floor) are ALL refuted for reducing MLP active bytes below q3 while generalizing. The ONLY unexplored path to fewer active bytes is DISTILLATION (train a smaller operator to match the function) -- a large training arc, not a compression of existing weights. 100 TPS (G22) and the TPS ladder remain BLOCKED, now on distillation as the sole surviving representation avenue.
reopen_if: a distilled/generated operator, trained to match the MLP function, achieves q3 quality at materially fewer active bytes held-out across layers, with Doctor holding.
